title: Add sustained latency eddy detector and rollback leash
author: Jordan Park
description: Motivation: transient spikes and throughput-coupled latency bumps are already handled by our existing canary detectors, but we observed production incidents where small sustained (minutes-long) latency elevations evaded windowed detectors and caused customer-visible degradation after cutover. This PR introduces the 'eddy' sustained-latency detector: a rate-decoupled, windowed detector that detects persistent latency elevation while resisting short bursts and throughput-driven noise. The detector implements: 1) rate-decoupling by normalizing latency fingerprints against a throughput-derived baseline per shard; 2) temporal persistence requirement (configurable consecutive windows) to avoid one-off spikes; 3) autocorrelation-aware smoothing to reduce sensitivity to periodic jitter; 4) configurable sensitivity knobs (window_ms, consecutive_windows, alpha smoothing). To prevent overreaction during a detected sustained regression, the PR also adds a 'rollback leash' controller that enforces gradual traffic rollback with a budget and cooldown (config knobs rollback_percent_per_minute, rollback_budget_tokens, cooldown_minutes). Implementation summary: added a new detector module perf_canary/detectors/eddy_detector.py (core algorithm + unit tests), integrated detector into the canary evaluator framework with feature flags, added leash control logic in perf_canary/leash_controller.go, plumbing for detector telemetry and traces (metrics names: perf.eddy.p50_delta, perf.eddy.sustained_windows, perf.rollback.leash_progress), and a Helm values flag to enable in clusters deploy/helm/perf-canary-values.yaml. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on staging for 48h with synthetic sustained-latency injection scenarios, canary on 1% traffic for 2h, then 10% for 4h, observe p95/p99 and rollback events. Test plan: unit tests for detector math, integration tests in tests/integration/test_eddy_probe.py that exercise rate-decoupling under varying throughput, and an end-to-end canary simulation harness run in perf-canary CI. Performance impact: detector is O(1) per shard per window; measured CPU delta on a staging prober ~0.15% and memory <10MB. Backwards compatibility: disabled by default; no breaking config changes. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/eddy-detector-design, Linear ENG-4821 is referenced in the PR. Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] CI green after re-run [x] docs (design + knobs) added.
